correctness.rationale: Open-neighborhood excess sum_v(c_S(v)-1)=3|S|-2n gives the sharp lower bounds and forces perfect covers to have no one-token exchanges because distinct prism vertices have different open neighborhoods. For even n the bipartition of the prism converts total domination exactly to two independent cycle-domination factors, with gaps between selected indices in {1,2,3}; the gap-defect 0,1,2 cases prove the factor graphs are isolated triples, a cycle, or a connected 4-regular graph of n(n+5)/6 vertices. Odd n=6k+1 has exactly one doubly dominated vertex; the explicit length-6 word repeated with one terminal column yields all 2n configurations through rotations/rim swap. Invertibility of the prism adjacency on these n makes the doubled vertex label unique. Legal exchanges map label a_i to b_{i+-3}, giving a connected 2-regular graph C_{2n}. Independent direct enumeration of all small prism total-dominating subsets at n=3..10 checked optimum counts and exchange degrees, including the deliberately unclaimed residue five. This finite check is only corroboration of the unrestricted gap/adjacency argument.

final_claim: For P_n=C_n square K2 and exchange of one selected vertex while retaining minimum total domination, T_n is 9 isolated vertices for n=0 mod 6, C_{2n} for n=1, C_n square C_n for n=2, 3 isolated vertices for n=3, and H_n square H_n for n=4 (mod 6), where H_n is connected 4-regular ordinary minimum-cycle-domination exchange graph with n(n+5)/6 vertices; n=5 mod 6 is excluded.
